exploring: Stated intent, hiring, task forces, or 'evaluating' AI — but no shipped internal use case yet.
piloting: Named pilots or limited deployments in specific teams, plus policy/governance build-out — not yet firm-wide production.
scaling: Multiple AI use cases in production across the firm, used daily, named as a strategic priority — but AI augments human decisions; humans still frame, guardrail, and make/verify the final call. AI is in the workflow. A single production use case that makes live investment decisions with material capital counts as scaling.
embedded: AI is structurally constitutive of how the firm operates, not just a tool within it: autonomous decisions without a human in the loop on each one, org structure actually redesigned around AI, and AI as the default mode with humans as the exception. AI IS the workflow. Currently UNREACHED — see note.
_scope_note: This dashboard measures OPERATIONAL/INTERNAL AI adoption — how a firm uses AI in its own investment process and operations. It excludes (a) AI products a firm sells to clients, and (b) AI as an investment thesis or portfolio holding.
_embedded_empty_note: No institution in this corpus meets the Embedded bar on the public record. The test is autonomous decisions with no human in the loop, an organisation actually restructured around AI, and AI as the default mode. For the institutions furthest along, the record points the other way: NBIM records human oversight of investment decisions as non-negotiable, CPP Investments that humans frame and verify every output, BlackRock that the AI-default workflow "isn't quite here yet", and GIC that its virtual investment-committee member evaluates and challenges proposals rather than deciding them. The column is empty because nothing on the record has met the bar, not because it is held empty. It fills when public evidence supports it.
